topic.title: Probabilistic Decision Making and Evidence Accumulation
topic.overview: Decisions under uncertainty combine prior expectations with evidence that arrives over time. This topic models perception, reward-guided action, and adaptive learning through Bayesian or related computational accounts. It also includes newer work on how confidence evolves during model reasoning, linking uncertainty assessment with the decision to continue computing or act.
topic.whyItMatters: A rational account can explain why the same evidence leads to different choices under different priors or reward structures. Such explanations require comparison with behavioral data rather than assuming that a normative model describes neural implementation. Computational confidence likewise needs validation against actual correctness.
topic.evolution: A 1993 foraging model connects predictive learning with neuromodulatory influences. In 2012, a partially observable decision model reconciles static and time-varying effects of prior knowledge. Later representatives study reliability and volatile learning; a 2026 reasoning analysis uses changes in token entropy to detect convergence and guide early stopping or trajectory selection.
openQuestions: When do confidence changes track reliable evidence rather than premature commitment?
Which experiments distinguish alternative ways of combining priors, sensory reliability, and reward?
